description: The per-call instruction limit (context.instructionLimit, ScriptHost.InstructionLimit) and the native stack guard. A script over the limit fails with kind 'interrupted', which pcall cannot catch; the context stays usable. spin(n) runs about 2n instructions (since the fused for-loop opcode; 10n before), so two spin(300000) calls pass only if each call has its own budget. Recalibrate n when the instruction count per iteration changes.

cases.name: a call under the limit returns
each call has its own budget
a call over the limit is interrupted
an endless loop is interrupted
cases.note: the error names the chunk and line where the script was stopped

cases.name: an endless numeric for loop is interrupted
an endless tail call is interrupted
cases.source:
local function f() return f() end
return f()

cases.name: pcall does not catch the interruption
cases.source:
local ok = pcall(function() while true do end end)
return 'after pcall'

cases.name: coroutine.resume does not catch the interruption
cases.source:
local co = coroutine.create(function() while true do end end)
local ok = coroutine.resume(co)
return 'after resume'

cases.name: a loop inside a CLR callback is interrupted
cases.source: return (string.gsub('x', '.', function() while true do end end))

cases.name: an __index function that indexes its own table is a C stack overflow error
cases.source:
local t = setmetatable({}, { __index = function(t, k) return t[k] end })
return t.x

cases.name: output printed before the interruption is kept
the context works after an interruption
recursion through a CLR callback is a C stack overflow error
cases.source:
local function f(s) return (string.gsub(s, '.', f)) end
return f('x')

cases.name: pcall catches a C stack overflow
Lua recursion is still a stack overflow error
cases.source:
local function f(n) return 1 + f(n + 1) end
return f(1)
